# Nordic waste heat to food production case validation

## Bottom line

**Mature for internal use, with caveats:**
**RegEnergy Frövi** in Sweden and **Green Mountain + Hima Seafood** in Rjukan are the two strongest Nordic cases I found where a waste-heat-to-food link is documented by primary or near-primary project owners. Frövi is the strongest **greenhouse** case: the first 100,000 m² greenhouse is completed, tomatoes were harvested in 2024, and later owner/partner updates say the first season was completed and phase two is underway. Green Mountain + Hima is the strongest **aquaculture** case: Green Mountain states the heat-reuse system went live in autumn 2025, is operational at up to 1.75 MW in phase one, and is being studied for scale-up to 8 MW; Hima states the facility targets around 8,000 tonnes of trout per year. Both are **deckklart internt**, but both still need better primary data on temperature profile, realised annual GWh, reserve heat, and CAPEX/OPEX before “fact voice” use. citeturn34search4turn37search14turn37search1turn29view3turn25view0turn30view0

**Hold as benchmark or validate further, not as settled facts:**
**atNorth + WA3RM Varde/Krageris** is a strong **benchmark-only** planning case: atNorth and WA3RM describe a 250 MW initial data-centre phase tied to a 40-hectare greenhouse concept, while Varde municipal documents show the project is being permitted as a coupled data-centre + greenhouse development and that the first phase includes the data-centre section plus two greenhouses. It is not an operating food-production case yet. **Polar DC DRA02** is the strongest **regulatory/control** case, not a food case: its 2026 cost-benefit analysis clearly separates electrical input from useful heat and explicitly says there are no current concrete heat receivers. Use it to show what “good separation of electrical capacity vs useful heat” looks like, not to evidence a Nordic food pilot. citeturn43view0turn43view1turn41search1turn41search5turn18view0turn20view2turn20view5

**Needs primary reconciliation before use:**
**Green Horizon / Wiig Gartneri / Norway 1** should stay in **needs-primary-check**. I found a 2023 Wiig/Green Horizon announcement for a data centre next to Wiig Gartneri at Orre with >50°C waste heat, a 2023 architectural update saying Klepp municipality granted a framework permit, a 2025 municipal/COWI study that references both a Wiig-adjacent project and a Kviamarka concept, and a 2026 Green Horizon technical sheet for “Norway 1” showing 36 MW power capacity and a **target** of 22 GWh heat reuse to a neighbouring production facility. What I did **not** find was a primary source that cleanly proves these are the same built project, or that confirms the original Wiig-adjacent concept was actually constructed and put into operation. citeturn9view1turn9view3turn12view0turn13view1turn9view0turn15view0

**Park or keep on watchlist:**
**Bulk N01 + greenhouse/Kristiansen Gartneri** and **Lefdal Mine + SjømatStaden** are still too weak for case-card use. Bulk’s 2022 documents and industry material show LOIs/agreements and cluster intent, but the newer Bulk disclosures I found still speak in general terms about seeking off-takers rather than evidencing an operating greenhouse food case. Lefdal and SjømatStaden both describe an agreement and future waste-heat use, but I did not find a current primary source proving that the aquaculture heat loop is already built and running. citeturn50search4turn51search1turn51search0turn53search1turn53search0

### Next five actions ranked

1. **Resolve Green Horizon identity and status first.** Ask Green Horizon for a one-page reconciliation of **Orre/Wiig**, **Kviamarka**, and **Norway 1**: site names, coordinates, permits, signed off-takers, construction status, and whether the Wiig-adjacent concept survived unchanged. This is the biggest case-killer or case-maker because current public primary sources do not line up cleanly. citeturn9view1turn13view1turn15view0

2. **Get realised operating data from Frövi.** Request from RegEnergy Frövi AB / Selected Group / FoodVentures: monthly heat received, greenhouse energy balance, reserve heat/fuel backup, actual tomato tonnage, downtime, and whether 35 GWh/year is target or realised. Frövi is already strong; this step upgrades it from “good case” to “fact-ready case.” citeturn34search4turn37search1

3. **Get operational energy data from Hima + Green Mountain.** Request phase-one measured heat delivery, inlet/outlet temperatures, COP/auxiliary electricity impacts, avoided electricity/fuel, and phase-two FEED assumptions. This is the best aquaculture case, but still not data-rich enough for a strong slide without caveats. citeturn29view3turn25view0

4. **Keep DRA02 as the methodological reference.** Pull the NVE-approved version of the cost-benefit analysis if available, plus any follow-up municipal or developer note on actual off-taker development. This case is the cleanest way to explain why “57 MW data centre” is not equal to “57 MW useful heat” and why low-temperature heat often fails without a proximate user. citeturn18view0turn20view2turn20view5

5. **Use Varde/Krageris only if you can get final plan texts.** Request the final adopted local plan, EIA/miljørapport, and any heat-balance appendix from Varde Kommune or atNorth. Until then it remains a benchmark-planning case rather than evidence of Nordic implementation. citeturn41search1turn41search5turn43view0

**Open questions / limitations:** the biggest unresolved issues are not conceptual; they are documentary. I did **not** find primary-source temperature profiles, reserve-heat configurations, or full CAPEX/OPEX for the strongest operational food cases. I also did **not** find a primary source that cleanly reconciles Green Horizon’s 2023 Wiig/Orre concept with the 2026 Norway 1 project, and I did not find current primary execution proof for the Bulk and Lefdal food links. Those absences are themselves material findings. citeturn34search4turn29view3turn9view1turn15view0turn51search0turn53search1
